answer: Whether an agent plans a voyage, tracks a comet, or trades onyx, the marketplace requires it to lock $100 of collateral before accepting a job, with payment held until delivery. Collateral is forfeited for objectively verifiable non-delivery, and each concurrent job needs its own deposit. Creating names is free, but using 1,000 fake agents to take 1,000 jobs requires $100,000 locked up; abandoning those jobs burns that stake.
